operation: §198 — structured-pipeline transport/binding remediation and successor-protocol preparation. Product-owner Option B.
terminalReason: The governed-binding capability is now ABSENT when no governed source is supplied and PRESENT with its exact sourceIds rendered when one is. The §197 rejection keyword is gone from every request before the adapter strip runs. The circuit breaker, the empty-run scorer invariant and the integrity-scan precision fix are implemented and regression-covered. The §196 K3 claim is corrected additively without editing its evidence. 89/89 §198 matrix, 72/72 source integrity, every legacy suite green. No provider call was made and no deeper contract problem was exposed.

PRODUCT_OWNER_DECISION_IMPLEMENTED.whyStrongerNotAWorkaround: a bounded field is still a field: the model is told the capability exists and the only thing stopping a populated one is a keyword this provider does not honour at all. BINDING_VISIBILITY.section197Defect: buildExpertUserPrompt renders governed records under opaque handles (R1, R2) with citations redacted and never shows a sourceId, while §196 asked the first pass to name one. The binding was unexercisable in principle.
BINDING_VISIBILITY.resolution: buildExpertVNextUserPrompt appends a removable AVAILABLE GOVERNED EVIDENCE block exposing the exact sourceId of every supplied record, and only supplied records.
BINDING_VISIBILITY.evidenceTextTreatment: still rendered through redactCitationTokens, exactly as v15 does
BINDING_VISIBILITY.whyTextStaysRedacted: the authorization requires the exact sourceId to be visible and requires citation containment OUTSIDE the authorized supplied evidence to be unchanged. It does not require the TEXT to carry citations, and showing them would be actively wrong: v15's HARD PROHIBITIONS still tells the first pass that reproducing a number from its own input is the same violation as inventing one, and §196 gave the first pass no supplied-source reuse allowance. A first pass shown a citation could only be punished for repeating it.
BINDING_VISIBILITY.residualStated: a first pass cannot quote a governed citation. That is v15's rule, not a §198 invention. The supplied-source reuse allowance lives on the VERIFIER path, where the record arrives with its citation intact — confirmed unaffected by case G4.
BINDING_VISIBILITY.reversible: removing the appended block reproduces buildExpertUserPrompt(input) byte for byte

REQUEST_COMPATIBILITY.method: all twelve §197 first-pass requests rebuilt offline under the remediated contract. Nothing sent.
REQUEST_COMPATIBILITY.WHAT_THIS_DOES_NOT_PROVE: that the provider ACCEPTS the request. §198 proves only that the request no longer contains a keyword this provider is known to reject. Only sending one can prove acceptance, and §198 sends none.

CIRCUIT_BREAKER.rule: STOP on two consecutive pre-inference rejections sharing a normalized signature
normalizationRemoves: quoted identifiers carrying a separator or digit
normalizationKeeps: the structural path including the tool index
CIRCUIT_BREAKER.theDecidingField: reachedInference — set from provider-returned usage and response shape, NEVER inferred from the HTTP status
CIRCUIT_BREAKER.inferenceTimeFailures: produce NO signature and cannot contribute to a streak; a single inference-reaching attempt BREAKS a streak
CIRCUIT_BREAKER.counterfactual: the §197 run would have stopped at 2 calls instead of 12
CIRCUIT_BREAKER.wiringIntoTheExecutor: DEFERRED TO THE SUCCESSOR SLICE. §197's executor is a historical instrument and was not modified.
CIRCUIT_BREAKER.defectFoundWhileWritingIt: the first normaliser replaced any quoted token of 8+ characters, turning "property 'maxItems' is not supported" into "property '{identifier}' is not supported" and making two DIFFERENT unsupported-keyword rejections look identical. Caught by case K2.

EMPTY_RUN_SCORER_INVARIANT.rule: completed model executions = 0 ⇒ no behavioural or semantic axis may emit a positive verdict
EMPTY_RUN_SCORER_INVARIANT.mechanism: axisResult and axisRatio CANNOT express one — on an empty denominator they return the empty-run state regardless of what the caller computed
EMPTY_RUN_SCORER_INVARIANT.hardFailEvaluability: returns anyTriggered: null, not false. false asserts the conditions were checked and held; null says the question was not askable.
EMPTY_RUN_SCORER_INVARIANT.selfAudit: emptyRunReportingViolations scans a scorer's own output for a CLASS of positive wording, not one remembered string
EMPTY_RUN_SCORER_INVARIANT.alsoEnforces: a single observation is reported as x/n literally with NOT_MEANINGFULLY_ESTIMABLE, never as a percentage; a zero denominator never renders as 0/0
EMPTY_RUN_SCORER_INVARIANT.section197ScorerItself: LEFT EXACTLY AS §197 PRODUCED IT. The correction is preserved in place; the invariant is made permanent in the shared module that future scorers import.

INTEGRITY_INSTRUMENT_PRECISION.defect: §197's gate failed 57/58 by grepping /TRANSITION_AUTHORITIES…MODEL/ and matching owed-fact-ledger.ts's own COMMENT explaining that there is deliberately no member for a model explanation
INTEGRITY_INSTRUMENT_PRECISION.correction: stripComments removes comments while preserving line numbering; STRING LITERALS ARE DELIBERATELY KEPT, because a forbidden token in a literal is executable content and hiding it would weaken coverage
INTEGRITY_INSTRUMENT_PRECISION.honestLimit: comment-stripping alone would NOT have rescued that check — the ledger also IMPORTS MODEL_AUTHORED_SOURCES nearby, so the naive proximity regex matches executable text too. Recorded as case O2b. The real fix was always asserting over the exported constant's VALUES.
INTEGRITY_INSTRUMENT_PRECISION.recorded: preferValueAssertion — where an invariant can be asserted against an exported value, assert the value; use a scan only where no value carries the property
